books.title: Kavero’s Little Laboratory
books.concept: Small, supervised experiments with everyday objects: Kavero makes bold predictions, gets funny surprises, and tries again. These are stories, not step-by-step experiment instructions.

stories.title: The Ice-Cube Overcoat
stories.summary: Kavero dresses an ice cube in a tiny woolly coat to keep it warm, then has to explain to Granny why the undressed cube melted first.

stories.title: The Bubble Blame Game
stories.summary: Pip blames the wind, his nose and Tuesday for bursting bubbles, until Kavero notices that his dry finger pops every bubble he tries to catch.

stories.title: The Pepper Traffic Jam
stories.summary: Floating pepper rushes away from a soapy finger, and Kavero appoints Granny traffic officer while he tries to work out where it can possibly park.

stories.title: The Balloon Hair Salon
stories.summary: A rubbed balloon lifts Kavero’s curls, but his new salon loses its only customer when Granny decides her hair is exciting enough already.

stories.title: The Raisin Swimming Club
stories.summary: Raisins bob up and down in sparkling water, leaving Kavero trying to award a swimming medal to a contestant that refuses to finish.

stories.title: The Penny Passengers
stories.summary: Kavero’s foil boat sinks under its tiny passengers; Poppy suggests a wider boat while Pip proposes giving the pennies swimming lessons.

stories.title: The Paper Bridge Queue
stories.summary: A flat paper bridge sags under a toy car, but folding it changes everything—except Pip’s insistence that the car needs a smaller lunch.

stories.title: The Hungry Paper Towel
stories.summary: Water creeps up a paper towel, and Kavero wonders whether Granny’s kitchen roll has been drinking without permission.

stories.title: The Magnet Job Interview
stories.summary: Kavero interviews a magnet for a tidying job, only to discover it picks up paper clips beautifully and ignores almost everything else.

stories.title: The Spinning Egg Audition
stories.summary: Granny gives Kavero a raw egg and a hard-boiled one to compare, and his spinning contest becomes a search for which contestant has a wobbly inside.

stories.title: The Orange Life Jacket
stories.summary: An orange floats with its peel on but sinks when peeled, spoiling Pip’s theory that swimmers should always take their coats off.

stories.title: The Missing Sugar
stories.summary: Sugar vanishes into Granny’s tea, and Kavero investigates a disappearance that Granny insists she can still taste.

stories.title: The Spoon Orchestra
stories.summary: Tapping glasses with different amounts of water gives Kavero different notes, but Granny keeps drinking the tune.

stories.title: The Stubborn Water Drop
stories.summary: Kavero tries to persuade a water drop to spread across waxed paper, while Pip names the little bead and asks whether it can stay for lunch.

stories.title: The Paper Helicopter Landing
stories.summary: Two folded paper spinners fall differently, and Kavero’s carefully marked landing pad remains the one place neither chooses to visit.

stories.title: The Biscuit Sound Test
stories.summary: Kavero discovers his own crunch sounds louder with his ears covered, then struggles to explain the experiment while Granny waits for him to finish chewing.

stories.title: The Upside-Down Seed
stories.summary: Kavero plants a bean upside down to confuse it, but its root grows down anyway and Granny declares the bean an excellent listener.

stories.title: The Shadow Puppet Giant
stories.summary: Moving a paper puppet nearer a torch makes its shadow enormous, and Toby worries their tiny theatre will need a much bigger door.

stories.title: The Paper Flower Surprise
stories.summary: Folded paper petals open on water, but Kavero’s grand introduction lasts so long that Granny’s flower finishes blooming before he gets to its name.

stories.title: The Bendy Pencil
stories.summary: A pencil looks bent in a glass of water, and Kavero keeps pulling it out to inspect it while Pip congratulates him on another successful repair.

books.title: Kavero’s School-Day Surprises
books.concept: Classroom projects, playground misunderstandings and small school responsibilities become warm comic adventures. Ms Reed guides without humiliation; Granny helps with preparations and hears the surprising results.

stories.title: The Show-and-Tell Pocket
stories.summary: Kavero forgets his show-and-tell object, then discovers that the contents of his pockets need more explaining than the object ever did.

stories.title: The Very Long Question
stories.summary: Asked to bring one question to class, Kavero joins six with “and,” leaving Ms Reed deciding where the first answer should begin.

stories.title: The Library Whisper
stories.summary: Pip’s enormous whisper carries across the library, so Kavero demonstrates a quieter one that nobody can hear—including Pip.

stories.title: The Plant Monitor
stories.summary: Kavero writes a daily report on the classroom plant, and his greatest challenge is making “still a plant” sound like breaking news.

stories.title: The Class Photo Gap
stories.summary: Kavero saves a space in the class photograph for an absent friend, inspiring the class to hold up their friend’s drawing in the gap.

stories.title: The Lost-Property Parade
stories.summary: Helping sort lost property, Kavero models three scarves and a tiny hat to find their owners, then cannot remember which scarf belongs to him.

stories.title: The Silent Line Leader
stories.summary: Kavero leads the class with elaborate hand signals, but the queue keeps stopping because everyone thinks he is starting a new game.

stories.title: The Giant Group Poster
stories.summary: Each friend draws a different part of their poster without comparing sizes, leaving a tiny town populated by one enormous duck.

stories.title: The Pencil-Case Concert
stories.summary: A rattling pencil case interrupts Kavero’s quiet reading, and every attempt to remove the noisy object starts a louder performance.

stories.title: The Almost-Finished Story
stories.summary: Kavero writes “The End” to finish his class story, then adds so many last-minute adventures that the ending needs its own page.

stories.title: The Classroom Tour
stories.summary: Showing a new pupil around, Kavero explains the best puddle and the squeaky step but forgets to point out their classroom.

stories.title: The Backstage Tree
stories.summary: Cast as a tree in the school play, Kavero prepares excellent leaves with Granny but must learn when a helpful tree should stop giving the actors directions.

stories.title: The Desk Treasure Map
stories.summary: Kavero maps his cluttered desk to find things faster, then has to ask Toby to help find the map.

stories.title: The Weather Reporter
stories.summary: Kavero’s school weather announcement lists every possible forecast, and Poppy suggests starting by looking out of the window.

stories.title: The Partner Drawing
stories.summary: Toby describes a picture while Kavero draws without seeing it, producing a remarkably cheerful elephant where a watering can should be.

stories.title: The Question Box
stories.summary: Kavero volunteers to collect anonymous class questions, but everyone recognises the six that begin “What if my puppy…”

stories.title: The Reading Relay
stories.summary: The friends take turns reading a funny scene aloud, and Pip gives the same enormous voice to the giant, the mouse and the narrator.

stories.title: The Thank-You Banner
stories.summary: Kavero makes a banner for the school caretaker, but his explanation of every helpful deed stretches beyond the paper and halfway across Granny’s floor.

stories.title: The Tidy Tray Trouble
stories.summary: Kavero sorts shared classroom supplies by colour, leaving Poppy hunting through five trays for five differently coloured pencils.

stories.title: The Best Part Report
stories.summary: Asked to write his favourite part of the school trip, Kavero chooses the bus conversation with Toby—and Granny helps him see why that counts too.

books.title: Kavero’s Party Plans
books.concept: Invitations, games, performances and little celebrations: Kavero tries to make everyone happy, while Granny helps him leave room for the guests to have ideas of their own.

stories.title: The Invitation Puzzle
stories.summary: Kavero draws party invitations without words, and Toby arrives with a pillow because the birthday cake looked like a bed.

stories.title: The Doorbell Committee
stories.summary: Everyone wants to welcome the first guest, leaving Granny to welcome the next five while the children rehearse their greeting.

stories.title: The Balloon Name Tags
stories.summary: Kavero gives each guest a name balloon, but the balloons drift between chairs and Dad spends lunch answering to Poppy.

stories.title: The Musical Cushion
stories.summary: There is one cushion for every player in Kavero’s friendly music game, yet Fozzy keeps choosing the one Kavero is about to sit on.

stories.title: The Treasure Map Mix-Up
stories.summary: Kavero draws a treasure map from his own viewpoint, sending his friends to the wrong side of every landmark until Granny turns it around.

stories.title: The Endless Welcome Speech
stories.summary: Kavero thanks everyone for coming, then thanks everyone for listening, while Pip wonders whether they should applaud to make him stop or keep him going.

stories.title: The Fancy-Dress Label
stories.summary: Nobody recognises Kavero’s homemade costume, so he adds helpful labels until Granny can no longer see what he is dressed as.

stories.title: The Magic-Wand Substitute
stories.summary: Kavero loses his pretend magic wand before his show, and Granny’s wooden spoon becomes a much funnier replacement when Pip expects it to produce soup.

stories.title: The Pass-the-Parcel Pause
stories.summary: The music stops on Granny, but she is so busy cheering for everyone else that the parcel completes another lap before she notices.

stories.title: The Birthday Chair
stories.summary: Kavero decorates a special chair for Mum, then has to remove half the decorations so the guest of honour can actually use it.

stories.title: The Smallest Parade
stories.summary: Millie wants a parade without a long walk, so Kavero leads a grand procession around Granny’s armchair and announces every lap as a new destination.

stories.title: The Guessing Jar
stories.summary: Kavero carefully counts every button for a guessing game, then adds one beautiful button and forgets whether he counted that one already.

stories.title: The Two-Person Dragon
stories.summary: Kavero and Toby make a two-person costume, but their dragon keeps walking towards two different party games.

stories.title: The Party Photographer
stories.summary: Kavero arranges perfect photographs while Granny catches the funny faces between poses, and everyone prefers her pictures.

stories.title: The Guest of Honour
stories.summary: Kavero organises a thank-you party for Mr Bell, who arrives ready to fix the decorations and has to be persuaded to put his toolbox down.

stories.title: The Rainy Garden Party
stories.summary: Rain sends Kavero’s garden party indoors, where a pretend picnic beneath the dining table becomes more popular than his original plan.

stories.title: The Applause Rehearsal
stories.summary: Pip teaches everyone a spectacular cheer for Granny’s entrance, but they practise so enthusiastically that she comes in early to see what she has missed.

stories.title: The Party Bag Puzzle
stories.summary: Kavero makes every party bag exactly the same, until Millie asks to swap her puzzle for the drawing Poppy would rather give away.

stories.title: The Last Game Vote
stories.summary: The guests vote for one final game, and Kavero discovers that everyone’s favourite is the silly waiting game they invented while he counted.

stories.title: The Morning-After Celebration
stories.summary: Tidying the party with Granny, Kavero finds a forgotten paper crown and declares her Queen of Finding Things Under Chairs.
